label: second input token of sequences starting with j
explanation: Fires at step t=1 (the second original token) if and only if the first original token is j, whatever the second token is. Dev precision and recall are both 1.0 with no counterexamples. It never fires at t=0 (on the j itself), at any later original step, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase, so it does not respond to j appearing anywhere else. Activation is nearly constant (mean 0.32, max 0.39). The small variation tracks the identity of the second token: p gives the max activation and i, c and s give the lowest (about 0.74 of max). Sequence length, digits and repeats do not change whether it fires.

issues: No refutation found. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0, mass recall 1.0, correlation 0.997. The misses tool on the test split lists 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The dev profile backs every factual claim. All activity is at t=1 (orig_idx 1). There are 0 activations at t=0, at t>=2, at the delimiter or in the copy phase. prev_tok and first_tok are always j. Magnitude has mean 0.321, median 0.317 and max 0.391. The top examples are all 'j p' at 1.00, and the lowest quartile is i/c/s at about 0.73-0.75.

Firing rate varies by L and n_digits only because t=1 is a smaller share of steps in longer sequences. Firing given (t=1, first=j) is 16441/16441, so it is unconditional on those variables. The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
